description:
Add a `--simulate` (alias `--stub-mode`) flag to the helper that, when set, replaces the real subsystems (PipeWire, encoder, segment writer, exporter) with deterministic in-process simulators that emit the JSON-RPC events and method responses exactly as a real capture/encode session would per N-007 §6 and §7. The point is to give T-014's preload wiring a real event stream to exercise, and to give T-010a's runner harness a deterministic counterpart it can validate the harness against before any real PipeWire code lands.

Scope (binding):
- Add `--simulate` to the helper CLI (parsed in `main.rs`). Default is OFF. When enabled, the helper logs `mode=simulate` at boot.
- Implement four simulators behind feature traits in the helper:
  1. `capture::sim::SimCapture` — fakes `capture.requestSession`/`startStream`/`stopSession`. On `startStream`, emits `capture.sessionReady` after 100 ms with a fixed `CaptureFormat { width: 1920, height: 1080, fpsNum: 60, fpsDen: 1, fourcc: "NV12", colorPrimaries: "bt709", range: "limited" }`. Emits `capture.diagnostics` at 1 Hz with monotonically increasing `total_produced` at 60 fps and `dropped_since_last = 0`. Pause/resume work and emit `streamPaused`/`streamResumed`.
  2. `encoder::sim::SimEncoder` — emits `encoder.probeResult` for `nvenc`, `vaapi`, `qsv`, `libx264` with the first one (configurable via `--simulate-encoder <name>`, default `nvenc`) selected. Emits `encoder.selected { backend, codec: "h264", encoderInputRect, encoderOutputFormat }` 50 ms after a session is ready. Emits `encoder.diagnostics` at 1 Hz with bitrate/queue depth counters.
  3. `segment::sim::SimSegmentBuffer` — emits `replay.segmentDiagnostics` at 1 Hz with `fragmentsReceived`, `segmentsCommitted` (one new segment per 2 s), `bytesOnDisk` (synthetic), `diskWriteLatencyMs` (constant 5 ms).
  4. `export::sim::SimExporter` — on `replay.save`, returns a `ReplaySnapshot` synchronously within 50 ms (well under the 250 ms + fragment-latency N-007 §15 / N-005 §15 bound). On `replay.export_start`, emits `export.queued` → `export.started { mode: "stream-copy", plan: { ... } }` → `export.progress` ticks (1 Hz, pct climbing linearly) → `export.completed { finalPath: "/tmp/sim-<exportId>.mp4", bytes: 12345678, sha256: "<deterministic>", durationS: <requested>, mode: "stream-copy", fpsObservedOut: 60.0 }`. Writes a real (empty or 1-byte) file at `finalPath` so downstream checks can stat it.
- Simulators MUST honour the FSM transitions in N-007 §8 — the renderer in T-014 must be able to round-trip every state (`IDLE` → `RECORDING` → `SAVING` → `EXPORTING` → `IDLE`) by calling the documented methods in the documented order. Any out-of-order call returns the appropriate JSON-RPC error from N-007 §17.
- Failure-injection knobs for T-010a:
  - `--simulate-fail capture.startStream=pipewire-state-error` → after 500 ms emits `capture.sessionLost { reason: "pipewire-state-error" }`.
  - `--simulate-fail encoder.probe=encoder-probe-failed` → emits `encoder.probeResult { result: "failed" }` for the requested backend.
  - `--simulate-fail export=ffmpeg-exited-nonzero` → during `export.progress`, emits `export.failed { reasonCode: "ffmpeg-exited-nonzero" }`.
  - `--simulate-fail segment=segment-sink-disk-full` → mid-session, emits `capture.sessionLost { reason: "segment-sink-disk-full" }`.
  - One `--simulate-fail` flag may be repeated to chain failures.
- All simulators feed through the same `transport::Notifier` from T-012; the JSON-RPC wire format is byte-for-byte the same as the real path.
- Add a tiny self-test: `cargo test -p cove-replay-engine -- --include-ignored simulate::round_trip` spins up the helper in simulate mode in-process, runs a full `requestSession` → `startStream` → `replay.save` → `replay.export_start` → `export.completed` cycle, and asserts the wire-format event sequence.

Out of scope (binding):
- No real PipeWire / ffmpeg / encoder code — those live in T-016..T-019.
- No new IPC methods or event names; only the existing N-007 §5/§6 surface is exercised.
- No renderer changes (T-014/T-020 own those).
- No Electron-side support for `--simulate`; the helper picks up the flag from its CLI. T-013's supervisor exposes a `helperExtraArgs` knob for dev (already a normal Node `spawn` array) — no special wiring required.
- No CI hooks.
- No write of `out.mp4.ffprobe.json` or `out.mp4.mediainfo.json` — the simulator only writes the placeholder `finalPath`. Real artefact validation is T-010a's harness against a real MP4 from T-019.

Acceptance criteria:
1. `./target/debug/cove-replay-engine --simulate --ipc-socket /tmp/test.sock --log-dir /tmp` runs and accepts a JSON-RPC client.
2. From a connected client, the full `requestSession → startStream → save → exportStart → completed` cycle returns valid responses and events within 5 s wall time at the synthetic 60 fps cadence.
3. `--simulate-fail capture.startStream=pipewire-state-error` produces `capture.sessionLost` with the matching reason code and the FSM-correct state transitions.
4. `--simulate-encoder libx264` selects `libx264` in the `encoder.selected` event.
5. `cargo test -p cove-replay-engine -- --include-ignored simulate::round_trip` passes.
6. The simulator code is gated behind a `#[cfg(feature = "simulate")]` or a runtime branch — it ships in dev builds and may or may not ship in release builds (implementer's choice; default = ship it, since T-010a relies on it).

Verification commands:
- `cargo build -p cove-replay-engine`
- `cargo test -p cove-replay-engine`
- Manual end-to-end: helper in simulate mode + the dev preload smoke harness from T-014 → verify a full cycle in DevTools.
- `git status --short`

Codex review expectations:
- Confirm the simulator emits events with the exact wire shapes from N-007 §6/§7 (no shortcut camelCase, no missing fields).
- Confirm FSM transitions are honoured (e.g. `replay.export_start` cannot complete before `replay.save` returns a `ReplaySnapshot`).
- Confirm failure-injection flags map to the reason codes documented in N-007 §17 and N-008 §6.
- Flag any leakage of simulator types into real subsystems (modules must be cleanly separable).
- Flag any test that exercises the wire format only via in-Rust types rather than through the actual length-prefixed transport — the round-trip test must use the same framing as the production transport.

Failure handling:
- If `cargo test --include-ignored` is unusual for this workspace, document the alternative invocation in the helper crate README rather than reshaping the test gate.

No commits, tags, or publishes from this ticket.
title: Add helper stub/simulation mode for validation harness
